messages.subject_clean: [knitr] get control over the names of the figures
messages.body_plain:
My suggestion is, spend more time on what Figure 1.1 is supposed to
visualize, and refrain from looking at the auto-generated filenames :)

If you really cannot sleep at night because of the annoying -1, you
may try to rename the figure file, e.g. (not tested)

library(knitr)
local({
  hook_plot = knit_hooks$get('plot')
  knit_hooks$set(plot = function(x, options) {
    name = sub('-1([.][a-z]{3,4})$', '\\1', x)
    if (name != x) file.rename(x, name)
    hook_plot(name, options)
  })
})

The release notes explained why -1 is necessary:
https://github.com/yihui/knitr/releases See the second bullet in the
section Major Changes of knitr 1.7

Regards,

messages.body_plain:
If using LaTeX, you want figure names to be symbolic in case you insert or remove a figure that would cause everything to be renumbered.  So you use the chunk label as the symbolic LaTeX label and use \ref{label} to refer to it.  You can even refer to symbolic labels in comments in R code, to state which figure the code produced.

Frank

Xtable creates as-is LaTeX within the knitted output, not external
files.  I would not call myself a knitr expert, but AFAIK the table
labeling has to be done by xtable, not knitr.

Semi-related... unlike the xtables package, note that the tables
package does not generate an environment, so you have to include the
label yourself in raw LaTeX when you create the table environment if
you use that package.

+++ patrick2.Rnw    2014-12-09 08:05:37.469152046 -0800
@@ -54,7 +54,7 @@

 \item
 The linear regression is displayed in Figure~\ref{fig:Figure1}
 \item

-The linear regression statistics are summarized in~\ref{Table1}
+The linear regression statistics are summarized in Table~\ref{Table1}
 \end{itemize}
 \end{frame}

@@ -64,12 +64,12 @@

 \begin{itemize}
 \item
 Use the \texttt{xtable} package to print nice \LaTeX\ tables:

-<<Table1, echo = FALSE, results = 'asis'>>=
+<<, echo = FALSE, results = 'asis'>>=
 library(xtable)
-  xtable(summary(lm(y~x))$coefficients, caption ="Regression summary")
+  xtable(summary(lm(y~x))$coefficients, caption ="Regression
summary",label = "Table1" )
 @

messages.subject: Rendering a table in latex when a rowname starts with [
messages.subject_clean: Rendering a table in latex when a rowname starts with [
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I am using knitr to produce PDF documents using pdflatex. I have to print a table which has chemical names as its rownames. One rowname starts with left square bracket [. I am trying to include this table in my knitr document using print(xtable(tab)), but latex fails to render this. Below I create a toy example to describe the issue. The following document doesn't render.

\documentclass{article}

\begin{document}

<<results='asis'>>=
tab <- matrix(rnorm(4), nrow=2)
rownames(tab) <- c("a", "[b]c")
colnames(tab) <- c("p", "q")
library(xtable)
print(xtable(tab))
@

\end{document}

One dirty workaround I found was to insert a line change character at the beginning of the rowname that starts with [. That is, the following document renders correctly:

\documentclass{article}

\begin{document}

<<results='asis'>>=
tab <- matrix(rnorm(4), nrow=2)
rownames(tab) <- c("a", "\n[b]c")
colnames(tab) <- c("p", "q")
library(xtable)
print(xtable(tab))
@

\end{document}

Therefore, in my real case the knitr code using this workaround is something like the following (which is just a generalization of the above by inserting \n wherever needed):

\documentclass{article}

\begin{document}

<<results='asis'>>=
tab <- matrix(rnorm(4), nrow=2)
rownames(tab) <- c("a", "[b]c")
colnames(tab) <- c("p", "q")

### I insert \n at the beginning of rownames that start with [
rownames(tab) <- gsub("^\\[", "\n\\[", rownames(tab))
library(xtable)
print(xtable(tab))
@
\end{document}

I tried to achieve this same workaround using sanitize.rownames.function as below (because I think that it is a slightly less dirty way of doing the same thing, as it wouldn't change the rownames permanently):

\documentclass{article}

\begin{document}

<<results='asis'>>=
tab <- matrix(rnorm(4), nrow=2)
rownames(tab) <- c("a", "[b]c")
colnames(tab) <- c("p", "q")

library(xtable)
print(xtable(tab),
  sanitize.rownames.function=function(x) { gsub("^\\[", "\n\\[", x) }
)
@
\end{document}

So, my questions are:

1. Is there a more elegant way (or a more automatic way) of solving this issue?
2. If my workaround is reasonable, how should I fix my sanitize.rownames.function?

Thanks a lot in advance.

Best regards,
Gopal

If you use LyX, you still need to click the preview button over and over again.

This problem can be easily solved by using three tools: a PDF viewer
that does not suck in terms of locking the pdf file (i.e. anything but
not Adobe Reader), a shell script, and GNU make. Something like

#!/bin/sh
while true;
  do make && sleep 1;
done

For make, you define how to compile .Rnw to .pdf (cf
http://kbroman.org/minimal_make/ if you are not familiar with make).
If you are using Windows, there must be something similar to the shell
script I typed above, and you need to figure it by yourself, or wait
